1  ORDER
With the consent of the parties, the appeals are heard finally.

These appeals are arising out of a common award dated 30.07.2019 passed by the Fourth Additional Member, MACT, District Dewas therefore, they are heard together and disposed off by common order.
2.

These appeals have been filed preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 30.07.2019 by the Fourth Additional Member, MACT, District Dewas in MACC Nos.170/2017 (M.A.No.5858/2019), 168/2017 (M.A.No.5864/2019), 201/2017 (M.A.No.5867/2019) and 205/2017 (M.A.No.5868/2019).

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 29.09.2016 the appellants were travelling in Tata Magic Pick up van bearing registration No.MP-09-LP-1916 3 MA-5867-2019 and on the way back, the respondent/driver while turning the vehicle at a turn, due to rash and negligent driving of driver,
the said pickup turned turtle resulting in injuries to the appellants.
4. Thereafter the appellants/claimants filed an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 before the claims tribunal for compensation.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 30.07.2019 passed by the claims tribunal the present appeals have been filed.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants in Misc. Appeal No.5867/2019 and 5868/2019 submits that the award passed by the learned tribunal is on lower side as the injured have received several injuries, therefore, he prays for enhancing the amount of Rs.20,000/- in M.A. No.5867/2019 and Rs.7,000/- in M.A. No.5868/2019.

6. In M.A.Nos.5858/219 and M.A. No.5864/2019, learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the income of the injured has been taken on the lower side and disability has also been reduced without any basis.

7. In M.A. No.5858/2019 income has been taken as Rs. 4500/- where as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh on the date of accident it should be Rs.6850/-.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Also permanent disability which is proved by disability certificate Exhibit P/15 issued by Dr. H.S. Rana (PW.2) at 20% however, the learned claims tribunal has considered the disability @7% for whole body, 4 MA-5867-2019 which should have been considered @ at least 8% for whole body.

He also submits that claims tribunal has also erred in not awarding any amount in the head of future prospects, whereas looking to the age of 58 years of the injured,
10% amount is to be added in the head of future prospectus on the date of the accident.
In the head of pain and suffering Rs.25,000/- has been awarded which is also on lower side, therefore, the same is to be enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
In the heads of special diet and attendant Rs.2000/- each has been awarded which has to be taken as Rs.5000/- under each head.
No amount has been awarded in Ku .

It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant be enhanced appropriately.

8. In M.A. No.5864/2019 income has been taken as Rs. 4500/- where as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh on the date of accident it should be Rs.6850/-.

He also submits that claims tribunal has also erred in not awarding any amount in the head of future prospects, whereas looking to the age of 35 years of the injured, 40% amount is to be added in the head of future prospectus on the date of the accident.

In the heads of special diet and attendant Rs.2000/-
5 MA-5867-2019 each has been awarded which has to be taken as Rs.5000/- under each head.
No amount has been awarded in the head of transportation, which should be considered as Rs.5,000/-.
Even the amount of loss of income for three months during treatment as assessed by the tribunal at Rs.13,500/- is on the lower side which needs to be enhanced to Rs.20,550/-.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant be enhanced appropriately.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer of the appellants/claimants on the ground that amount awarded on all the heads in all the appeals have been addressed properly hence no interference is warranted and prayed for dismissal of the appeals.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
11.

In Misc. Appeal Nos.5867/2019 and 5868/2019 looking to the injuries sustained by the injured appellants, without going into the nicety of the computation of the amount, the award amount is enhanced and the appellant/claimant is entitled for an additional lump sum amount of Rs.20,000/-
in M.A. No.5867/2019 and Rs.7000/- in M.A. No.5868/2019.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the claims tribunal.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
Findings as to pay and recover shall remain intact.

Since the appeal M.A. No. 5867/2019 has been valued at Rs.50,000/- and M.A. No.5868/2019 has been valued at Rs.25,000/- the court fees has accordingly been paid therefore, the remaining court fees is to be 6 MA-5867-2019 paid within a period of 30 days as per the prevailing slab from the date of filing of the appeal.
In case the appellant fails to pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days then beyond 30 days interest will not be payable till filing of the Court fees.

12. In M.A. Nos.5864/2019 and 5858/2019 , it is not in dispute that where proper evidence is not available for assessing the income of the deceased / injured it should be taken as per the circular/guidelines issued under the Minimum Wages Act.
In the present cases, it comes to Rs.6,850/- on the date of accident ie., on 29.09.2016.

Considering the aforesaid disability certificates,
the permanent disability is taken as 3% in M.A. NO.5864/19 and 8% in M.A. No.5858/19.
13.

In M.A.No.5864/2019 the appellant is entitled for the following enhanced amount :-
Rs.92,064/-
 Permanent disability  (Rs.1,15,080 x 5% x 16)

Attendant Head Rs.5,000/-
 Special diet Rs.5,000/-
 Transportation Rs.5,000/-
 Medical Expenses Rs.23,970/-
 Loss of income for 3 months Rs.20,550/-

Thus just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.1,76,584/-
(enhanced amount of Rs.1,76,584/- amount awarded by 7 MA-5867-2019 Tribunal of Rs.93,390/-).
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.83,194/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the claims tribunal.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
Findings as to pay and recover shall remain intact.

14. In M.A.No.5858/2019 the appellant is entitled for the following enhanced amount :-
Rs.65,102/-
 Permanent disability  (Rs.90,420 x 8% x 9)
 Pain and sufferings Rs.30,000/-

Attendant Head Rs.5,000/-
 Special diet Rs.5,000/-
 Transportation Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of income for 3 months Rs.20,550/-
 Total Rs.1,30,652/-.

Thus just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.1,30,652/-
(enhanced amount of Rs.1,30,652/- amount awarded by Tribunal of Rs.76,520/-).
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.54,132/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the claims tribunal.
